video.title: I Picked Draper to Win It All (because of 3 patterns you can practice tomorrow)

classification.reason: The coach analyzes pro match footage of Jack Draper, Joao Fonseca, and Rafael Nadal to teach three high-margin singles patterns for viewers to practice.

problem.title_as_question: Why do players take high risks without getting rewards, and what patterns create high-margin dominance?
problem.definition: Players frequently hit high-risk, flat shots that yield minimal tactical reward, or conversely slow down their swing when trying to play safe, creating poor risk-reward ratios.

symptoms.description: Hitting extremely hard, flat groundstrokes that slow down on court and leave the rally in the exact same state despite high risk taken.
Decelerating the racket and hesitating on swings when attempting to play safe or patient.
Committing unforced errors by attempting overly aggressive low-percentage shots when pushed on defense.

causes.statement: Players hit the ball excessively hard and flat without extracting any meaningful tactical advantage or winner from the effort.
Players misinterpret playing with margin and patience as an instruction to slow down their swing speed.
Shot selection suffers from poor risk-to-reward ratios, opting for high-difficulty flat shots where the potential reward does not justify the risk.
Players grant opponents too much respect on defense and attempt wild bailout shots rather than hitting high, safe balls back into court.

angles.summary: Using racket head speed to hit high over the middle and lowest part of the net creates massive margin for error without sacrificing depth.
Clarifying that playing with margin does not mean slowing down the swing; swinging fully without hesitation is necessary to generate spin.
Rafael Nadal demonstrates that offensive play should rely on height and heavy spin to big targets rather than risky flat slapshots.
Contrasting Fonseca's high-difficulty, low-reward offensive shots against Jack Draper's effortless, high-margin pattern that consistently forces errors.

solutions.summary: Commit to a full swing without hesitation, directing racket head speed upward over the lowest part of the net rather than slowing down.
solutions.external_goal: hit high over the middle of the net

solutions.summary: Play aggressive groundstrokes with generous height and heavy spin toward large court targets instead of going for low flat winners.
solutions.external_goal: big target down the line with height and spin

solutions.summary: When stretched on defense, lift the ball high over the middle into the court to reset the point and make the opponent earn every winner.
solutions.external_goal: high over the middle of the net into the court

solutions.summary: Track your risk-reward ratio during play, and immediately discard difficult shots that do not yield significant advantages.
